prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single “best” roofer in Denver from a live search right now, but I can help you find the best contractor for hail damage quickly and safely. Two options — tell me your ZIP code and whether this is residential or commercial and I’ll tailor recommendations and a short checklist; or use the guidance below to vet roofers yourself.

How to pick the best roofer for hail damage
- Check certifications and experience
  - Manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc.).
  - Experience with hail claims and Xactimate/insurance scopes.
- Licensing, insurance and local standing
  - Company registered in Colorado and a local address or long-term presence in the Denver metro.
  - Current general liability and workers’ comp insurance — ask for certificates.
  - Good BBB rating and consistently positive Google/Yelp reviews (look for recent storm-related jobs).
- Warranties and materials
  - Written workmanship warranty plus manufacturer shingle warranty transferability.
  - Use hail-resistant products as appropriate (impact-rated shingles, Class 4 options).
- Claim handling and transparency
  - Will provide a full, line-item estimate (not just a single price) and show the Xactimate line items if they’re billing insurance.
  - Clear policy on assignment of benefits — be cautious about signing AOBs.
- Red flags / storm-chaser signs
  - No local address, only a cellphone, or heavy pressure to sign immediately.
  - Unwilling to provide proof of insurance or references.
  - Offers to waive your deductible or asks you to sign over insurance checks without clear contract terms.

Questions to ask every roofer
1. How long have you done hail damage repairs in Denver? Can you provide recent references and photos?
2. Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
3. Will you provide a full, line-item estimate and work with my insurance adjuster?
4. Do you handle permits and inspections?
5. What warranties do you offer (workmanship and materials)?
6. Can I see proof of general liability and workers’ comp insurance?
7. Who will manage my job on site and what is your cleanup policy?

Practical steps
1. Get at least 3 written estimates (line-item). Compare scope and materials, not just final price.
2. Document damage with photos/videos and your insurance claim number.
3. Verify references and recent comparable jobs in Denver.
4. Don’t sign anything you don’t fully understand (especially AOBs).

If you want, I can:
- Draft an email/call script and a comparison table to send to 3–5 roofers.
- Help you evaluate 2–3 contractor proposals (if you paste them here).
- Give a short list of highly recommended local companies if you provide your ZIP code and I can suggest how to look them up.

Which would you prefer?
